newsitem.title: USA: Kensey Nash partner recalls some Angio-Seal.
newsitem.headline: Kensey Nash partner recalls some Angio-Seal.

text.p: Kensey Nash Corp said Tuesday its marketing partner, Sherwood-Davis & Geck, is voluntary recalling selected lots of the Angio-Seal hemostatic puncture closure device effective immediately.
Sherwood-Davis is a subsidiary of American Home Products Corp and Kensey Nash's licensee for the device.

Kensey Nash said the action was taken because the companies have identified a potential for a very low incidence of damage to a component of the device during the assembly process at the manufacturing facility of Sherwood-Davis' affiliate, Quinton Instrument Co.
Kensey Nash said the potential damage may result in an unexpected break of the suture during product use.
Modification of the manufacturing process is now being done to correct the problem, it said.
The recall involves devices from six lots distributed in the United States and three lots distributed in Europe and is believed to involve less than 1,000 devices, Kensey Nash said.
It said it expects new supplies of the Angio-Seal device will be available in the United States within sixty days.

International product supply should not be affected by the recall, as the majority of this product is made by Kensey Nash, with final assembly at the Sherwood-Davis & Geck facility in Tullamore, Ireland, it said.

In addition, clinical trials will not be affected as those devices are manufactured by Kensey Nash. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and appropriate international regulatory authorities have been advised of the recall, it added.
Earlier, Smith Barney downgraded Kensey Nash to neutral from buy based on the recall, said analyst Melissa Wilmoth.
"We consider it a temporary problem and we think it's a good product but we need to see that the company can manufacture this properly."
She said the period the product will be off the market "basically pushes our (earnings) estimates out by a quarter."
Kensey Nash was off 2-7/8 to $12.00 in mid-afternoon trading.
